topic_title: Top 10 Dog Breeds That Barely Shed
intro: Low-shedding coats come in three types. Hairless breeds, like the Chinese Crested, lose very little hair but need skin care. Curly coats, like Poodles and Bichons, trap loose hair, so it stays off your sofa but mats without regular brushing. Long, silky coats, like the Havanese, Yorkie and Shih Tzu, grow continuously and shed little, but tangle easily. Allergens come from skin, saliva and urine too, so spend time with a breed before buying if allergies are the reason you're looking.

picks.description: The Shih Tzu has a long, silky double coat that sheds little but tangles quickly, so brush daily or keep it in a short clip with regular grooming. It is the calmest dog on this list, with low exercise needs of around 20 to 30 minutes a day, and it is affectionate and friendly with children and other pets. Shih Tzus can be stubborn about house-training. Their short muzzle makes them sensitive to heat, and their eyes need regular cleaning.
picks.best_for: Calm households wanting a low-energy, low-shedding lap dog
picks.quirky_fact: Shih Tzu means little lion in Chinese.
picks.skip_if: You want a quick learner or live somewhere very hot

picks.description: The Yorkshire Terrier has a fine, silky coat, closer to human hair than fur, that sheds little. A long coat needs daily brushing; many owners keep a short puppy cut with trims every six to eight weeks. Yorkies weigh about 4 to 7 pounds and are bold, affectionate and energetic. They bark a lot, which matters in apartments, and they can be moderately hard to house-train. Their small size makes them fragile around rough play. Dental care is important, as with most toy breeds.
picks.best_for: Adults wanting a tiny, bold, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: Yorkies were originally bred to catch rats in clothing mills in northern England.
picks.skip_if: You need a quiet dog or have rough young children

picks.description: The Miniature Schnauzer has a wiry, dense coat that sheds little. It needs weekly brushing and clipping or hand-stripping every six to eight weeks, with the beard wiped after meals. Minis weigh 11 to 20 pounds, are easy to train and get along with children and other pets. They need about 45 minutes of activity a day. They are alert watchdogs and will bark at visitors, so early training on a quiet cue helps.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a sturdy, low-shedding small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Hand-stripping keeps a Schnauzer's wiry coat texture; clipping softens it over time.
picks.skip_if: You want a quiet dog at the door

picks.description: The Bichon Frise has a soft, curly coat that sheds very little onto floors. It needs brushing most days and a professional trim every four to six weeks to prevent mats. At 12 to 18 pounds, Bichons suit apartments, and they are cheerful, easy to train and good with children and other pets. Energy is moderate. House-training can take longer than average, and they dislike being alone for long stretches.
picks.best_for: Apartment dwellers wanting a cheerful, low-shedding companion
picks.quirky_fact: A Bichon's coat has a soft undercoat and a curly outer coat, which gives it a plush feel.
picks.skip_if: You won't brush daily or pay for regular grooming

picks.description: The Havanese has a long, silky coat that sheds little but tangles easily, so brush several times a week or keep it in a short puppy clip with regular professional trims. At 7 to 13 pounds, it is sturdy, cheerful and easy to train, and it gets along with children, cats and other dogs. Energy is moderate, met with a couple of walks and indoor play. Havanese often live 14 to 16 years. They are very people-oriented and can develop separation anxiety if left alone for long periods.
picks.best_for: Homes where someone is around often and wants a small, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Havanese are the national dog of Cuba.
picks.skip_if: The dog will be alone for long workdays

picks.description: The Lagotto Romagnolo has a dense, woolly curly coat that sheds little. It needs regular brushing and a clip every couple of months to stop the curls from cording or matting. Lagottos weigh 24 to 35 pounds, have moderate energy and a famously good nose, bred for truffle hunting, so scent games keep them content. They are affectionate, good with children and other pets and fairly trainable. At 14 to 16 years, they are long-lived.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a medium, low-shedding dog that loves nose work
picks.quirky_fact: Lagottos can be trained to find truffles, and some owners do it as a hobby.
picks.skip_if: You won't commit to regular clipping

picks.description: The Standard Poodle is the best large dog on this list for anyone avoiding dog hair. At 40 to 70 pounds it is athletic, intelligent and easy to train, and it is good with children and other pets. It needs about an hour of exercise and mental work daily. The curly coat sheds very little but needs frequent brushing and professional grooming every four to eight weeks. Mature Standards are calm and dignified indoors.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a large, trainable, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Standard Poodles are often used as the Poodle parent in larger doodle crosses.
picks.skip_if: You can't budget time and money for regular grooming

picks.description: The Miniature Poodle, around 10 to 15 pounds, offers the same low-shedding curly coat as the Toy in a sturdier body that holds up better with children. Expect brushing several times a week and a professional trim every four to eight weeks. Minis are intelligent and energetic, needing about an hour of walks, play and training daily, and they get along with children and other pets. Without enough activity they can get noisy or anxious.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a small, sturdy, low-shedding dog
picks.quirky_fact: Poodle coats grow continuously, which is why they need clipping rather than seasonal shedding.
picks.skip_if: You want a low-energy dog or minimal grooming

picks.description: The Toy Poodle's tight curls trap loose hair, so very little ends up on floors or furniture. That coat needs daily brushing and a trim every four to six weeks, which you can keep short and practical. At 4 to 6 pounds, Toys suit small homes, but they are energetic and very intelligent, so they need daily walks plus training games. They are affectionate and easy to train and get along with other pets. Their small size makes them fragile around rough play, so they suit adults or homes with older children.
picks.best_for: Adults wanting a tiny, clever dog with almost no shedding
picks.quirky_fact: Toy Poodles commonly live into their mid-teens.
picks.skip_if: You have toddlers or can't keep up with grooming

picks.description: The Chinese Crested comes in two types: hairless, with silky hair only on the head, tail and feet, and the fully coated Powderpuff. The hairless type sheds the least of any breed on this list, but its skin needs care: sunscreen on sunny days, a sweater in cold weather and regular moisturizing or bathing to prevent acne. The Powderpuff needs brushing several times a week. Cresteds weigh 8 to 12 pounds, have moderate energy and are affectionate, gentle and good with children and other pets. They bond closely with their people and dislike being left alone for long.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting the least possible hair and a cuddly small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Hairless and Powderpuff puppies can be born in the same litter.
picks.skip_if: You don't want to manage sunscreen, sweaters and skin care

faqs.question: Which dog breed sheds the least?
faqs.answer: Hairless breeds such as the Chinese Crested and the Xoloitzcuintli shed the least because they have little or no coat. Among coated dogs, Poodles of all sizes, the Bichon Frise and the Lagotto Romagnolo hold loose hair in their curls and shed very little onto floors.

faqs.question: Are low-shedding dogs hypoallergenic?
faqs.answer: No dog is fully hypoallergenic. Allergens come from dander, saliva and urine, not just hair. Low-shedding breeds spread less hair and dander around the house, which many people with mild allergies tolerate better. Meet the breed, and ideally the individual dog, before committing.

faqs.question: Do low-shedding dogs need more grooming?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Curly and long, silky coats keep growing and trap loose hair, so they need brushing several times a week or daily and professional trims every four to eight weeks. Hairless breeds swap brushing for skin care like sunscreen and moisturizing.

faqs.question: What is the best low-shedding dog for families?
faqs.answer: The Standard Poodle and Bichon Frise are strong family picks: friendly, easy to train and good with children. The Havanese and Miniature Schnauzer suit families wanting a smaller dog. All need regular grooming to stay comfortable and mat-free.

faqs.question: What is the best large dog that doesn't shed?
faqs.answer: The Standard Poodle is the most common choice for a large, low-shedding dog. Other options include the Giant Schnauzer and the Portuguese Water Dog. All three need regular professional grooming and plenty of daily exercise.

seo_title: 10 Dog Breeds That Barely Shed (2026 Guide)
answer: The Chinese Crested, Toy Poodle and Miniature Poodle shed the least of the breeds here: the hairless Crested drops almost no hair, and Poodle curls hold loose hair until it is brushed out. The trade-off with nearly every low-shedding breed is grooming, often a professional trim every four to eight weeks. No dog is completely allergen-free.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for breeds with low shedding, then ordered them by how little loose hair each tends to leave around a home, noting grooming effort, energy and temperament so you can weigh the upkeep.
